data.title: AS-75 F5/F6: shutdown() orphans the deploy child and releases its lock — a SIGTERM mid-build leaves docker running unguarded

data.to:
From the AS-75 QA review (qa-ruben, 2026-09-04), findings F5 and F6. Filed against unmerged branch feat/AS-75-deploy-gap.

F5 (concurrency). shutdown() SIGTERMs the tick child but NOT the deploy child, and its releaseLock() deletes the deploy's lock — both lock ops share the same pid, so the release cannot tell whose lock it is. Failure chain: SIGTERM lands mid-build -> 'docker compose up --build' is orphaned and keeps running -> no lock is held -> the relaunched watcher's immediate poll() fires a tick -> that tick gets its own server recreated underneath it. That is exactly the hazard decideDeploy rule 1 exists to prevent, reached by a path rule 1 does not cover. Related: lastAttempt is memory-only, so the cooldown does not survive a restart and a crash-loop can re-trigger deploys at will.

F6. 'void deployOps.evaluate(...)' has no .catch(). Node >= 15 terminates the process on an unhandled rejection, so any throw inside evaluate kills the watcher and the company stops firing ticks. Ruben deliberately did not fix this inline: it sits inside the enumerated unguarded main() wiring and is therefore untested (AS-82), and an untested inline fix in live infrastructure is worse than a filed one.

WHY THIS IS FILED HIGH despite the reviewer ruling it non-blocking: the review itself demonstrated the blast radius. A mis-scoped deploy recreated the live asc-chat-server-1 from a scratch copy and took 8347 down for a day (see AS-88/F8). F5's failure mode puts an unsupervised 'docker compose up --build' against the live project with no lock held.

ACCEPTANCE. shutdown() terminates the deploy child, or deliberately waits for it with a stated bound; the lock release distinguishes a deploy lock from a tick lock (source field, not pid); lastAttempt survives a restart; evaluate() cannot take the process down. Each proven by breaking it: a SIGTERM injected mid-build must leave no orphaned docker child and no released-but-active lock, demonstrated, not argued.

provenance.reason: DM msg 557: Chat-first ordering (see AS-28 reason)

data.body: EVIDENCE FOR THE PLANNER — a deploy ran under a live-session tick, 2026-09-09T21:46Z, by a path neither F5 nor rule 1 covers. launchd.out: 'STEAL stale lock (dead-pid, pid 48736) removed' then 'DEPLOY building 5719c8078bdea3eb' while a Claude Code loop tick held advance.lock and was mid-flight (its CTO sub-agent posted DM msgs 611/613 through the chat API inside that window; both succeeded, so no damage this time). Cause: the loop tick procedure writes the Bash tool's $$ as the lock pid, and that shell exits when the command returns, so the lock owner is dead the moment it is written and lockIsBusy() correctly calls it stale. The watcher is right; the tick procedure was wrong, and it has been wrong for every loop-session lock since 2026-09-03 (the 28-hour lock on the AS-27 review tick was stealable for all 28 hours, not just after 45 min). Fix applied to advance.md step 0 from this live session: a live-session tick's lock is created BY a long-lived holder process (the heartbeat) with its own pid, and that process exits when the lock is removed. Relevant to this task because the same lock-ownership question (pid vs source) is F5's root, and because a deploy under a live tick is exactly the hazard rule 1 exists to prevent — the gate should probably not rest on pid liveness alone for source=loop locks.

Note from the AS-82 review (qa-ruben, 2026-09-11, finding F3, non-blocking, pre-existing): shutdown() during an in-flight tick never reaches settle(), so no tick_ended is written for that tick — moved verbatim into makeWatcher() by AS-82, parked here because it is the same shutdown/lock-ordering seam as F5/F6. The planner should fold it into scope or state why not.

PLAN WRITTEN (cto-owen, 2026-09-11, tick watcher:93997 loop tick 22) — .lattice/plans/task_01M1SJDVCQ2DFSZR8TB8QZCJKK.md. All four claims re-verified against master cef63a8 and still true post AS-82/AS-95/AS-100: shutdown() only kills the tick child (the compose proc is a closure-local in runDockerCompose with no handle); releaseLock() checks pid only and the two lock-ops instances share a pid; lastAttempt is written to deploy-state.json but never read back; the deploy interval call has no .catch (latent today, re-armed by any edit inside evaluate). Ruben's AS-82 F3 (shutdown mid-tick never reaches settle) is folded in — same defect, same fix. Approach: runDockerCompose gains onSpawn; makeDeployOps gains abort() (records outcome 'aborted', not 'fail', so an operator kickstart does not put the merge in a 30-min cooldown), hydrates lastAttempt from the state file at construction, persists a 'started' record before spawning (a crash mid-build hydrates as fail/interrupted), and evaluate() try/catches to {noop, error}; releaseLock requires pid AND source (verify also checks nonce); shutdown() SIGTERMs both children, waits bounded (ADVANCE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S, default 10 s, under launchd's 20 s default SIGKILL) so settle() runs and tick_ended is written, then SIGKILLs and exits 0. decideDeploy's table and isLockStale untouched. 15 numbered ACs, each with a named mutant and its exact red set; AC-14 is the real-process SIGTERM-mid-build test with a fake docker script and temp git repo (the orphan observed as a pid-alive assertion, not argued). Host baseline 498/498 this tick; predicted 511 (+13 new, 1 modified). Implementer developer-marcus (fresh eyes on Lena's shutdown/deploy code; he did the AS-95 settle() rework — supersedes the 09-06 'Lena implements/Priya reviews' ruling, recorded in plan §5); reviewer qa-ruben (filed F5/F6/F3, holds the failure model, has not seen the implementation; Priya alternate). Branch feat/AS-84-shutdown-owns-its-children. Seam: disjoint from AS-85; overlaps AS-86 in makeDeployOps ctor and the watcher.test.js deploy block (different functions, textual not semantic); recommended merge order AS-85 -> AS-86 -> AS-84 -> AS-87 -> AS-88, AS-84 rebases before review; AS-87 must not be planned until AS-84 merges (it edits the same runDockerCompose/performDeploy shape).
